newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Fall in Japan sidelines Singapore rubber players.
newsitem.headline: Fall in Japan sidelines Singapore rubber players.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market finished weakly on Thursday with many players sidelined by the sharp fall in Japanese prices and the belief that prices will probably probe lower levels, dealers said.
People were also sidelined due to the Moslem Eid Al-Adha holiday on Friday which will close down markets in Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia, dealers said.

"A lot of people retreated to the sidelines after Japan fell so sharply," a dealer said, refering to the long liquidation in Tokyo which sent the benchmark September rubber contract reeling by 3.4 yen to end at 135.9 yen.
"Buyers feel prices will come off some more after Japan's slide so they decided to sit it out. Offtake was very light today," another dealer said.
Dealers said the market will probably suffer further next week due to soft consumer sentiment. The only sign of buying in the market was some shortcovering for RSS3 grade rubber.

At around 0945 GMT, June RSS3 was seen at 112.00-114.00 U.S. cents a kg from 112.50 cents. May RSS1 was seen at 158.00-160.00 Singapore cents (US$1.09-$1.11) a kg from 160.00 cents. October/December TSR20 was seen at 110.00-112.00 U.S. cents a kg from 112.00 cents. -- (US$1-S$1.44) Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
